To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sediment plays a key role as a source of nutrients and OM to water column, which can have bottom up effects on pelagic food webs.
sediment quality affects the pelagic food webs in a bottom-up manner, but only in the absence of top-down controls (fish).

the addition of two contrasting lake sediments at the bottom of replicated large mesocosms led to moderate changes in pelagic food web communities and stoichiometry but not in lipid composition, despite differences in the potential biodegradabilty of the sediments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the bottom up effects of lake sediments on pelagic food webs.
the role of sediments as a source of nutrients and organic matter to the water column and their potential effects on the structure and function of pelagic food webs.
the influence of sediment on the pelagic community of lakes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sediment plays a major role in the internal cycling of nutrients and organic matter in lakes, but its effects on pelagic food webs are not straightforward, and depend on the sediment quality.

the sediment plays a key role as an internal source of nutrients and OM, but that its bottom up effects on pelagic food webs are not necessarily obvious and depend on the sediment characteristics and the pelagic food chain.
sediment quality (e.g. biochemical composition) can affect the pelagic food webs, but the effects depend on sediment quality and on the pelagic community.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sediment is a source of OM for pelagic communities but that the influence of this sediment OM on these communities depends on the quality of sediment OM.
sediment quality has a moderate impact on the pelagic communities, and this impact can be modulated by fish predation.
sediment plays an important role in the pelagic food webs and that the biochemical composition of the sediments could influence the pelagic food chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sediment OM quality is a key driver of pelagic food web structure and functioning, but its influence remains poorly understood.

the bottom up effect of sediment on the pelagic compartment is limited to changes in the biomass, stoichiometry or lipid composition of pelagic compartments, but not in their elemental or biochemical composition.
the biochemical composition of lake sediments has to be taken into account to understand the bottom up control of the pelagic food webs.
